reader.requirement: At level 2 (the level this compiler implements for Relative I-O) a REWRITE of a relative file must succeed when the replacing record's character positions differ from the replaced record's, in every access mode and for every way the length is set (RECORD VARYING DEPENDING ON, an ODO record, several record descriptions without a RECORD clause); the level-1 equality rule and its 44 (§1985:VIII.1.3.4 d 2) do not bind a level-2 implementation.

edition-consulted.switches: passes the dialect year into FileConnector.Edition; RelativeConnector.Rewrite and Stored never read it (no comparison against the replaced record's length exists at any edition)

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|DialectLevel|DialectBehavior over RelativeConnector.cs, KeyedConnector.cs, FileConnector.cs#Stored, KeyedIoEmitter.cs#EmitRewrite; the only edition reads in RelativeConnector are the WRITE key-range behaviour and the sharing facility, neither on REWRITE's length path.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: l1c25_rewrite_length_differs covers random access with DEPENDING ON (relative and indexed); sequential access with an ODO record and a file with two record descriptions and no RECORD clause are not exercised

probes.printed: dynamic access, no RECORD clause, 01 X(8) and 01 X(20): C1 REWRITE long over short ST=00, C2 REWRITE short over long ST=00, rereads R1 [MMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMM] R2 [TTTTTTTTNNNNNNNNNNNN]; sequential access, VARYING 4 TO 30, ODO record 5 -> 27 chars: V2 ST=00, V3 CNT=25 [25ZZZ...]
probes.expected: 00 for every length change (level 2); a later READ returns the new record (the area past a shorter record is undefined per the READ rules)

citations.check: OK  §1985:VIII.4.6.4 GR3  (4.6.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR3

reader.notes: No code compares the replacing record's length with the replaced one for a relative file; FileConnector.Stored only applies the RECORD VARYING bounds (GR12) or pads a fixed record to the file width. The level-1 sentence is the only part a level-2 compiler does not apply; the probe shows success at --std 85 for growth and shrink in dynamic and sequential access.
reader.at-2023: gr3a at --std 2023 prints the same lines

refuter.evidence: Attacked the record-size forms the reader did not try: format 3 RECORD CONTAINS 8 TO 20 (implementor-defined fixed or variable, §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR13) with 01 X(8)/01 X(20) in random access, growth 8->20 and shrink 20->8 through REWRITE FROM a 3-character identifier; and format 1 RECORD CONTAINS 20 with a 4-character 01 rewritten over a 20-character record in sequential access. rf3a.cob at --std 85: C1 ST=00, C2 ST=00, R1 [MMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMM], R2 [WWW     ]; F1 ST=00, FR2 [ZZZZQQQQQQQQQQQQQQQQ] (the fixed record keeps the record area past the short 01, which the text leaves open). No 44 at level 2 for any length change, as the rule's level-2 sentence requires. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VIII.4.6.4 GR3  (4.6.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR3'; 'OK  §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR13  (3.8.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR13'.
